content.tldr: Migrating existing Parquet datasets to Iceberg can be performed in-place using metadata-only migration (CALL snapshot or CALL migrate) without rewriting underlying data files.
content.simple_explanation: Migrating petabyte-scale Hive Parquet tables by rewriting all data files (`INSERT OVERWRITE`) is prohibitively slow and expensive. Iceberg provides in-place migration procedures: `CALL catalog.system.snapshot('db.table', 'db.iceberg_table')` creates a shadow Iceberg table referencing existing Parquet files in-place. Once verified, `CALL catalog.system.migrate('db.table')` replaces the Hive table completely. Existing files are indexed into Iceberg manifests with zero data copying.
content.real_world_example: Installing modern barcoded catalog tags on existing warehouse shipping containers: rather than repacking goods into new boxes, staff affix digital RFID tags to existing boxes and register them in the digital warehouse database.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: While snapshot migration is instantaneous, historical files retain legacy directory partitioning. After migration, engineers should execute partition evolution and gradual background compaction.
